notice.title: How GlobalLinkup Curated Commerce Works
notice.body: Every piece is curated by the GlobalLinkup team, so members cannot list their own items. Adding merchandise happens in the admin portal, not here. If you make something and want it featured, send an artisan partner inquiry and our staff handles the listing, logistics, customs and direct payment.

drawer.howToOrderBody: GlobalLinkup facilitates orders personally with our regional makers. Because quantities are limited and made in small batches, orders are confirmed directly via our multilingual concierge. No shopping cart checkout or user reselling.

hero.badge: A quiet network for cultural exchange
hero.body: Discover real people, share your world, and reach across cultures. No feed algorithms, no cold messages, no contact details exchanged without permission.
hero.cardAlt: Sofia Martínez, photographed on a sunlit street in Barcelona.
hero.name: Sofia Martínez, 27
hero.bio: Curious about brutalist restoration, sunlit terraces, and analog film walks through the Gothic Quarter. Looking for genuine exchange across Spanish and English perspectives.

steps.title: A natural way to connect
steps.body: No endless swiping or unsolicited messages. A respectful ritual built around shared interests, native languages, and real conversation.
steps.step1Body: Read real dossiers: languages spoken, places lived, and what people actually spend their time on. Every profile is reviewed by a human before it goes live.
steps.step2Body: Press Connect with intent. There is no open message box and no way to cold-call anyone. Your request simply registers as waiting.
steps.step3Body: The person you asked reviews your dossier on their own time and answers yes or no. Declining costs nobody an awkward conversation.
steps.step4Body: Only after you both agree does the locker open: verified social channels, exchanged in the open because you chose it.

people.body: Verified members and local voices across Latin America, Europe, and beyond. Every persona is reviewed by a human before it goes live.

camila.alt: Camila photographed among plants in Medellín, Colombia.
camila.name: Camila Restrepo, 26
camila.quote: Leading wild indigo dyeing workshops in Santa Elena with grandmothers, and weekend trail runs through Arví park.

mateo.alt: Mateo photographed in a sunlit café in Mexico City.
mateo.name: Mateo Silva, 30
mateo.quote: Working in Roma Norte on clay acoustics. Eager to meet visiting creatives and show them lesser-known modernism and mezcalerías.

lucas.alt: Lucas in a bookshop in San Telmo, Buenos Aires.
lucas.name: Lucas Benítez, 32
lucas.quote: Based in San Telmo amid dusty tango vinyl records and old cinemas. Let’s drink mate and browse Sunday fairs for record-store treasures.

dispatches.title: Field Dispatches & Travel Chronicles
dispatches.body: Unfiltered photography and cultural observations shared chronologically.
dispatches.featuredAlt: A rustic ceramics workshop in Triana, Seville.
dispatches.featuredTitle: "Finding the last wood-fired kiln maestro along the Guadalquivir."
dispatches.featuredBody: We sat with Don Ramón, whose hands have turned Spanish clay for fifty years. No digital orders or mass production—just the smell of wet earth, orange blossoms drifting from the courtyard, and deep discussions on how traditions survive.
dispatches.featuredQuote: "El barro enseña paciencia antes que belleza."

mini1.title: "Morning copal incense and slow woven rebozos in Teotitlán."
mini1.body: I spent dawn watching cochineal insects turn natural wool into deep crimson. If you visit, skip the tourist vans and ride the collective taxi with maestro Pedro.
mini1.author: Elena V.

mini2.title: "Hut-to-hut through the Lenga forests during early autumn."
mini2.body: Winds howling across Refugio Frey, hot polenta cooked on an iron stove, and five different nationalities singing folk chords by firelight.
mini2.author: Joaquín S.

mini3.title: "Flamenco rhythm echoing off white lime walls at midnight."
mini3.body: No tickets or stadium lights. Just neighbors clapping bulerías on the stone terrace overlooking the Alhambra.
mini3.author: Marcus & Ana

marketplace.title: Artisan Goods & Nomadic Essentials
marketplace.body: Direct from heritage workshops across Mexico, Colombia, and Spain. No dropshipping, no markup exploitation.

bag.name: Veg-Tanned Saddle Leather Tote
bag.body: Crafted by Maestro Emiliano in San Martín Tilcajete. Hand-cut and sewn with heavy waxed linen thread for decades of travel.

ceramics.alt: A clay water pitcher beside coffee cups.

coffee.alt: Coffee cups and roasted beans on a wooden table.
coffee.name: High-Altitude Honey-Process Coffee
coffee.body: Single-estate Castillo beans from Jericó. Sun-dried in cherry with notes of cacao and wild panela. Roasted in small batches.
